purpose: Test whether V97-V106 LoadLeast initializer changes fail because they occur during ordinary pre-burst queue growth and persist into later burst windows, rather than being activated only after a causally observed arrival shock.

v106_mechanism_diagnosis.activation_locality: Material outcome changes concentrated in E888. Most E887/E889 scenario-seed pairs were assignment- or outcome-equivalent to the V94 anchor.
v106_mechanism_diagnosis.timing: Every accepted V106 window occurred at frame 180-501. The spike and sustained candidates made their first accepted changes before their registered burst intervals, while pulse accepted changes overlapped its first shock.
v106_mechanism_diagnosis.interpretation: Static queue-density gating can alter persistent container and queue state before any burst evidence exists. V107 admits the same outcome-blind resource-safe substitutions only after a shock is observed from past and current request arrivals; scenario labels and future arrivals remain unavailable.

closed_axes.global_density_threshold_refitting: closed by V101 and not reopened
closed_axes.resource_bottleneck_sum: less protective than resource Pareto in V106 and not advanced

hypothesis.primary: LoadLeast substitutions can be useful for burst recovery but unsafe when applied during ordinary pre-burst queue growth. Requiring a causal recent-arrival shock before bypassing the static upper-density gate should prevent pre-burst trajectory changes while enabling resource-safe redistribution when the observed workload has actually changed.
hypothesis.arm_a: Activate for 100 frames when the most recent 20-frame first-seen-request rate is at least 1.5 times the preceding 80-frame rate.
hypothesis.arm_b: Activate for 100 frames when the most recent 20-frame first-seen-request rate is at least 2.0 times the preceding 80-frame rate.
hypothesis.falsification: The hypothesis fails if neither candidate passes every paired throughput and both QPR gates in all three E3 scenarios on the complete fresh E890-E892 cohort.

allowed: request identifiers first observed by the online scheduler at or before the current frame
the scheduler's bounded 100-frame first-seen-request count history
immutable captured DAG edges and per-function CPU/output size
current collected and placement-feasible player set
current same-window CPU and memory headroom, locality, warmness, queue, bandwidth, and partial assignment state
frozen tape, SLA, reference, and V94 certificates
forbidden: completion count, throughput, latency, cost, QPR, SLA, or request completion status
future arrivals or future container and child placement state
workload scenario or burst label, seed identity, or registered burst interval as a routing input
confirmation-seed outcomes before a training pass
information_boundary.arrival_definition: A request contributes exactly once, at the first scheduling frame in which its ReqId is present; an append-only seen-ReqId set prevents completions or removals from changing past arrival counts.
information_boundary.shock_definition: After exactly 100 frames of history, compare integer counts in the preceding 80 frames and current 20 frames. Require both windows to contain at least 20 first-seen requests and compare rates with exact integer cross-products; zero or incomplete baselines fail closed.

candidate_mechanism.history_windows: 80 baseline frames immediately followed by 20 recent frames
candidate_mechanism.activation: arm for the current frame through current_frame+99 whenever the exact causal rate comparison passes
candidate_mechanism.density_policy: retain the nonterminal queue-density floor of 8; while shock-active, do not apply the closed static upper-density threshold; while inactive, dispatch the exact V94 anchor
candidate_mechanism.input_and_downstream_locality: retain V104 scalar, input-locality, warm-preservation, and current-warm-child downstream-locality checks
candidate_mechanism.resource_safety: retain V106 resource Pareto: CPU and memory headroom each nonworse
candidate_mechanism.coordination_acceptance: exact frozen V94 dual window-safe routed-expert, OCS, and immutable-baseline-welfare noninferiority guard without a LoadLeast window certificate
candidate_mechanism.exact_anchor_invariant: Before sufficient history, without a detected shock, or without an accepted resource-safe substitution, dispatch exactly V94 for identical current state and candidates.
candidate_mechanism.reference_policy: policy-independent offline reference construction remains unchanged

per_window: arrival-shock active flag and activation-until frame
critical-frontier protection and resource rejection counts
load_least gate evaluated/accepted/reason and substitution counts
performance fields retained but not opened before blind audit

selection_rule.throughput_gate_per_scenario: candidate three-seed mean is at least the matching V94 anchor mean and candidate-minus-anchor is nonnegative on at least two of three seeds
selection_rule.qpr_gate_per_scenario_per_convention: candidate three-seed mean is strictly greater than the matching V94 anchor mean and candidate-minus-anchor is strictly positive on at least two of three seeds
selection_rule.E3_winner_requires: one candidate passes all three metrics in all three E3 scenarios
selection_rule.multiple_passers: maximize the minimum relative mean QPR gain, then minimum relative throughput change, then prefer the stricter 2.0 shock threshold, then arm_id
selection_rule.absolute_formal_n20_baseline_gates: diagnostic only and never used to select a V107 profile
